name: Coastal interior
summary: The airy summer-house room by the sea. White and sand-coloured walls, white-washed or grey-oiled wood, linen slipcovers and woven rope or rattan; one sea blue carries the accents, and the room opens to the water and the light.

philosophy.core_thesis: A house by the sea takes its colours from sand, water and weathered wood, and its comfort from loose, washable fabric.
design_principles: Paint walls in white or sand at a light reflectance value of 75 or more, and panel one wall or the ceiling in painted tongue-and-groove boards.
Use white-washed or grey-oiled oak or pine with a weathered, matt surface.
Cover seats in loose linen or cotton slipcovers in white, sand or pale blue.
Add woven texture: rattan, wicker, jute, sisal and rope, at most one piece of each in a group.
Keep one blue family for the accents, from pale sky to deep navy, at 10% of the surface or less.
Open the room to the view: low furniture in front of the window and light curtains that pull fully clear.
anti_patterns: Theme objects: anchors, life rings, shells on every surface, 'beach' word signs
More than one blue family, or blue together with a second strong hue
Tall furniture that blocks the window view

composition.plan_logic: Seats face the water or the window wall. A large slipcovered sofa and two woven chairs stand on a jute rug; the dining table sits near the glass.
composition.focal_point: The window and the view of the water; inside the room, a white-painted panelled wall or a stone fireplace.

rules.rule: Make the view the focal point. Turn the sofa toward the window or set it at 90 degrees to it.
Balance the sofa with two woven chairs and a floor lamp on the other side of the rug.
Show the repeat of the panel boards on one wall or the ceiling.
Keep walls and floor close in value; give the edge with navy or with a dark rope line.
rules.value: wall to floor LRV difference 25 or less

rules.rule: Group objects in 3: a glass bottle, a stoneware jug and a piece of driftwood or coral.
Layer from the room to the water: seats, a low table, the window, the view.
Leave the window wall and the floor in front of it free.
Mark each zone with a jute or flat-weave rug.
Keep the route from the door to the terrace door clear.
Keep every piece in front of the window below the sill.
rules.value: 0 pieces above the sill on the window wall

rules.rule: Give white and sand the walls and large seats, weathered wood and natural fibre the secondary share, and one blue family the accents.
Let daylight lead; in the evening use woven or glass lamps at warm white.
Use one weathered wood and one blue family; vary only the weave of the fibres.
Shoot the room level, with a two-point view toward the window and the water.

zoning.circulation: One route from the door to the terrace door, and a loop around the dining table.

palette.distribution: White and sand on walls, ceiling and the large seats; weathered wood, jute and rattan as the secondary share; one blue family on cushions, a stripe, glass and ceramics; brushed nickel or rope as the thin line.

lighting.strategy: Daylight from large windows leads. In the evening, woven and clear-glass lamps give low warm pools.
lighting.daylight: Large windows and a glazed door to a terrace; linen curtains that pull fully clear. Window glass is 25% of the floor area.

layers.source: large windows and a glazed terrace door
floor lamp with a linen shade

materials.finish: Matt and weathered: white oil or lye on wood, matt paint, washed linen. Nothing is glossy.
materials.texture_contrast: Smooth painted boards against coarse fibre and loose linen, at about 1:1 by area.

furniture.silhouette: Deep, low, slipcovered seats; light woven chairs; simple painted or weathered wood frames.
furniture.arrangement: A large slipcovered sofa and two rattan chairs on a jute rug face the window; a long wood table with mixed chairs sits by the glass.

textiles.pattern: Plain linen and one wide stripe or ticking in blue and white; no more than one pattern in a group.
textiles.windows: Unlined white linen curtains on a simple rod, pulled fully clear of the glass by day.

objects.approach: Few objects that come from the place: glass, stoneware, driftwood, one boat or sea print. No theme decor.
objects.grouping: Groups of 3 on a sill or a sideboard; one large print or painting of the sea, not a gallery wall.

implementation.brief: A white summer-house living room with painted panelling and white-washed oak floorboards. A sand linen sofa and two rattan chairs stand on a jute rug in front of large windows to the sea; a rattan pendant hangs over a long oak table.
implementation.image_prompt: Coastal summer-house living room, white painted tongue-and-groove panelling, white-washed oak floorboards, large windows to the sea, sand linen slipcovered sofa, two rattan lounge chairs, jute rug, blue and white striped cushions, woven rattan pendant over a long white-washed oak table, clear glass bottles, soft bright daylight, airy, editorial photograph
implementation.negative_prompt: Anchors, life rings, shell clutter, beach word signs, dark wood, velvet, gloss, chrome, several strong colours, tall furniture in front of the window.
implementation.camera: 24 mm lens, camera at 120 cm, two-point view toward the window and the water.
implementation.scene_3d: Room 600 x 450 cm, ceiling 270 cm. Bright sky through two 220 x 200 cm windows and a glazed door; 3 point lights at 2700 K at 60, 140 and 200 cm.

emotion.target_response: Holiday calm: the viewer feels sea air, bare feet on wood and a house that does not mind sand.

avoid_when: The brief asks for drama, luxury or a dark, enclosed mood.
The room has no daylight to lead the scheme.

modifiers.how: Change the blue accents to grey wool and black lines, drop the rattan to one piece, keep the pale wood and the white walls.
Change the jute to a wool-silk rug and the slipcovers to tailored linen, add one stone surface; keep the sand and white palette.
Remove the stripe and the blue, add one dark wood and a low bench, reduce objects to 1–3 per surface.

sources.title: Ralph Lauren Home, Home Collection catalogues (1983 onward)
